templates.name: Cumulative Trail
sceneStructure: Setup: hero, situation, and goal are introduced together.
Encounter 1: hero meets/finds the first piece; the refrain is spoken.
Encounter 2: hero meets a second piece, and the refrain repeats while restating everything found so far, in order.
Encounter 3: hero meets a third piece; the cumulative restatement grows again.
Pattern break: the expected next repetition does not simply add another item â€” something unexpected interrupts the chain.
Discovery: the accumulated trail, seen all together, reveals the true belief.
Resolution: the goal is reached because of what the whole trail added up to, not any single piece.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: a short refrain restating the growing list of everything discovered so far ("And what could this be?")
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each occurrence must literally re-list every prior item plus the new one, in the same original order, drawn from the Blueprint's resolved storyActions/obstacle/world details â€” never a shortened or reworded restatement
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: at the pattern break, the refrain is interrupted mid-list rather than completed, signalling the accumulation is about to mean something rather than simply grow

templates.storyMechanic: Each new encounter adds itself onto a repeating, growing sequence of everything found/met so far, until the pattern breaks and the accumulated trail itself becomes the discovery.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is additive, not increasingly difficult â€” each encounter makes the list longer and the refrain longer to say, building anticipation through length and rhythm.
templates.turningPoint: Placed at the pattern break, immediately after encounter 3, when the hero notices the accumulated trail forms a shape or meaning rather than being a random list.
templates.resolutionPattern: The resolution is caused by seeing the whole trail at once (all prior encounters together), not by any single encounter being 'the answer'.

templates.name: Refrain & Change
sceneStructure: Problem: hero names the false belief for the first time, framed as the refrain.
Refrain 1 (unchanged): hero repeats the exact same line after a first attempt fails.
Attempt: hero tries again, differently than before.
Refrain 2 (unchanged): the exact same line returns after a setback, now carrying more weight.
Setback: the hardest version of the obstacle appears.
Pause: hero stops instead of repeating the pattern a third time as-is.
Refrain changed: the same phrase returns, but the wording has evolved to reflect the true belief.
New action: hero acts from the changed refrain and succeeds.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: the hero's own spoken false-belief line, restated near-verbatim from the Blueprint's belief.falseBelief
repetitionPattern.variationRule: the first three occurrences must be identical or near-identical in wording â€” only the surrounding scene changes, not the line itself
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: the fourth and final occurrence (REFRAIN_CHANGED) rewrites the line using the Blueprint's belief.trueBelief, keeping the same sentence shape so the change is audible (e.g. 'I can't do this yet' becomes 'Maybe I can try differently')

templates.storyMechanic: A single spoken phrase returns three times across the story, unchanged in wording at first, but its meaning shifts as the hero's situation changes â€” until the final repetition evolves in wording to show the belief has changed.
templates.escalationPattern: Each time the refrain repeats, the emotional stakes around it rise, while the words themselves stay flat â€” the tension is between unchanging language and a worsening situation.
templates.turningPoint: The pause beat, placed after the second setback and before the refrain changes â€” the hero must consciously stop repeating the old line rather than simply trying harder.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is proven by the refrain itself changing, not by a separate narration of growth â€” the transformed sentence IS the evidence of change.

templates.name: Question Chain
sceneStructure: Opening question: hero asks the first question, tied directly to the false belief.
Clue 1: hero finds a partial answer that only raises a new question.
Question 2: the new question is spoken aloud, more specific than the first.
Clue 2: another partial answer, again raising a sharper question.
Question 3: the question is now close to the heart of the true belief.
Clue 3: the final clue directly unlocks the revelation.
Revelation: all three questions resolve at once into the true belief.
Resolution: hero acts on the revelation to complete the mission.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: a short spoken question stem (e.g. "But why...?")
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each question must be strictly narrower/deeper than the one before it, tracing a single throughline toward the true belief rather than three unrelated questions
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: the third question is answered not by a new clue but by the hero already knowing â€” the answer comes from within, signalling readiness for the revelation

templates.storyMechanic: Every answer the hero finds creates a new, deeper question, so the story moves forward through curiosity rather than obstacles â€” the chain of questions itself is the plot.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is intellectual/emotional specificity, not physical difficulty â€” each clue narrows the mystery rather than raising the danger.
templates.turningPoint: The revelation beat, where the three clues suddenly connect and the true belief becomes obvious in hindsight.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is an 'aha' â€” the mission is completed as a direct, almost immediate consequence of finally understanding, not through further struggle.

templates.name: Circle Back
sceneStructure: Mirror opening: hero encounters X for the first time.
Old reaction: hero responds to X using the false belief.
Middle journey: hero has 2-3 experiences that challenge the false belief.
Insight: hero begins to understand the true belief, away from X.
Mirror ending: hero encounters a situation deliberately similar to X again.
New reaction: hero responds this time using the true belief â€” described using language that echoes the old reaction's scene for direct comparison.
templates.storyMechanic: The opening and ending scenes deliberately mirror the same situation, but the hero's reaction has transformed â€” showing change through repetition of circumstance rather than narration.
templates.escalationPattern: The middle journey escalates emotionally as each of the 2-3 experiences chips further away at the false belief, building toward the insight.
templates.turningPoint: The insight beat, positioned as far as possible from both mirrored scenes, so the contrast between old and new reaction is maximized.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is the mirror ending itself â€” the reader should be able to directly compare the opening and closing scene and see the transformation without being told about it.

templates.name: Hidden Clue
sceneStructure: Plant 1: an ordinary-seeming detail is shown, without being explained as important.
Plant 2: a second small detail is shown, also unexplained.
Rising problem: hero faces the real obstacle, seemingly unrelated to the plants.
Recall: hero suddenly remembers one of the planted details ('Wait... I've seen that before').
Payoff: the planted detail directly solves or reframes the problem.
Resolution: hero succeeds using the recalled clue, and the true belief is spoken.
templates.storyMechanic: Two or three apparently insignificant details are planted early in the story; later, one of them turns out to be exactly what the hero needs, and the payoff is only satisfying if it traces back to something genuinely shown before.
templates.escalationPattern: Tension escalates through the rising problem alone; the plants themselves stay quiet and low-key so they don't telegraph their own importance.
templates.turningPoint: The recall beat â€” must be traceable, in the actual text, back to Plant 1 or Plant 2, never to information introduced for the first time at the payoff.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is proof of attention rewarded: patience and noticing, not force, are what solve the problem.

templates.name: Three Guides
sceneStructure: Setup: hero states the problem, carrying the false belief.
Guide 1: offers an action-based response to the same problem.
Guide 2: offers an emotional/perspective-based response, different in kind from Guide 1.
Guide 3: offers an unexpected insight that reframes the problem itself.
Hero choice: hero synthesizes something of their own from all three, rather than adopting one guide's answer wholesale.
Resolution: hero's own chosen path succeeds, and the true belief is spoken in the hero's own words.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: the hero asking each guide the same underlying question, reworded to fit the guide
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each guide's response must differ in KIND (action vs. feeling vs. insight), never three variations of the same type of advice
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: there is no repeated final line â€” instead the hero's own choice beat replaces a fourth repetition, showing synthesis rather than imitation

templates.storyMechanic: Hero meets three different characters who each respond to the same problem in a different way (action, emotion/perspective, unexpected insight); the hero must choose their own path rather than simply copying any one guide.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is in depth of understanding, not danger â€” each guide brings the hero closer to the true belief without any guide stating it outright.
templates.turningPoint: The hero-choice beat, immediately after Guide 3, where the hero must actively decide rather than default to the most recent guide's advice.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must show the hero's own synthesis, not a direct copy of any single guide's suggestion â€” this is what proves growth rather than obedience.

templates.name: The Repeating Mistake
sceneStructure: Mistake 1: hero makes the mistake for the first time, driven by the false belief.
Ignore: hero brushes past the consequence without reflecting.
Mistake 2: the same mistake happens again, in a new but recognizable situation.
Notice: hero, or someone nearby, points out the pattern for the first time.
Mistake 3 (avoided): the same trigger appears a third time, but this time the hero catches themselves before repeating it.
Pause: hero stops mid-pattern, using the pause craft technique.
Understand: the true belief surfaces as the reason the old pattern kept happening.
Change: hero acts differently, breaking the pattern for good.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: the recognizable trigger situation that sets off the mistake
repetitionPattern.variationRule: the trigger must be recognizably the SAME kind of situation each time (same shape of provocation), while the surrounding context varies, so the pattern is legible to a young reader
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: the third occurrence of the trigger does not produce the mistake â€” it produces the pause instead, which is the whole point of the template

templates.storyMechanic: The same mistake happens two or three times, but each repetition increases the hero's awareness of the pattern, until the hero notices, pauses, and consciously changes instead of repeating it a final time.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is in the hero's growing self-awareness, not in the mistake's severity â€” mistake 2 should already carry a flicker of recognition that mistake 1 did not.
templates.turningPoint: The pause beat, placed at the third trigger, is the entire turning point of the template â€” it must visibly interrupt the expected third mistake.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is defined by the pattern being broken on-page, in front of the reader, not merely described afterward.

templates.name: Smallest Strength
sceneStructure: Big expectation: hero (or others) assumes the problem needs a big, loud, obvious action.
Big attempt fails: hero (or another character) tries the big action and it does not work.
Quiet quality noticed: hero notices a small, quiet quality in themselves that seemed unrelated to solving anything.
Quiet action: hero uses that quiet quality directly on the problem.
Resolution: the quiet action succeeds where the big attempt could not, and the true belief reframes strength itself.
templates.storyMechanic: Everyone (including the hero) expects the solution to require a big, obvious action; instead, the actual solution requires a quiet quality the hero already has (patience, listening, kindness), which is revealed to be powerful precisely because it was underestimated.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is expectation-based: the story keeps implying the quiet quality is irrelevant, right up until it becomes the entire solution.
templates.turningPoint: The 'quiet quality noticed' beat â€” the moment the hero (or the story) stops dismissing the small strength and starts trusting it.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must explicitly show the quiet quality succeeding where the big/loud attempt failed, so the inversion is legible, not just implied.

templates.name: Before / After Words
sceneStructure: Phrase (beginning): hero states the internal phrase in its false-belief form ('I have to ___').
Middle event: hero faces the situation and struggles under the false-belief framing.
Phrase (middle): the phrase returns, softened into a tentative, exploratory form ('Maybe I could ___').
Turning event: something small shifts the hero's understanding.
Phrase (ending): the phrase returns a third time, now stated as the true belief ('I can ___').
Resolution: hero acts fully from the final phrase and succeeds.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: a single internal sentence stem, unique to the Blueprint's belief, that keeps the same grammatical shape across all three uses
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each occurrence must keep the same sentence shape/subject so the three lines can sit side by side and clearly read as one evolving sentence, not three different thoughts
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: the third occurrence must be the Blueprint's belief.trueBelief itself (or a direct paraphrase preserving its meaning), not merely a more confident version of the false belief

templates.storyMechanic: A repeated internal phrase changes its wording three times across the story, tracking the belief shift directly through language rather than through plot events.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is entirely internal/linguistic â€” the external plot stays modest so the phrase's evolution stays the clear focus of the story.
templates.turningPoint: The turning event, placed between the middle and ending phrase, is intentionally small and ordinary â€” the point of this template is that a small event is enough once language starts shifting.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is proven by the hero speaking/thinking the final version of the phrase and then acting on it in the same beat.

templates.name: The Countdown
sceneStructure: Countdown 3: the limited resource (time/tries) is established at its highest number.
Countdown 2: hero rushes, the false belief driving hurried action, resource drops.
Pressure peak: with the resource nearly gone, panic-driven urgency is at its highest.
Pause choice: hero must choose to spend part of the remaining resource on stopping, not acting â€” this is the risk at the heart of the template.
Countdown 1: with the resource almost exhausted, hero acts once, wisely, from the true belief.
Resolution: success comes from the wisely-timed final action, not from speed.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: the countdown marker itself, spoken or shown as the resource decreases ("3... 2... 1")
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each countdown number must be paired with a distinct emotional state (confident, panicked, deliberately calm) so the numbers alone chart the hero's internal arc
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: the final count (1) is delivered slowly/quietly rather than urgently, deliberately breaking the accelerating rhythm the first two counts built

templates.storyMechanic: A limited number of attempts or amount of time (3-2-1) creates escalating urgency, but the turning point is the hero learning WHEN to pause rather than simply moving faster.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is literal and numeric â€” the resource visibly depreciates, and urgency should be felt to genuinely rise from 3 to 2.
templates.turningPoint: The pause-choice beat, where the hero must choose to 'spend' scarce resource on pausing â€” the risk of this choice not paying off must feel real.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must make clear that the pause was what made the final action work, not that the hero simply got lucky with the last attempt.

templates.name: The Almost-Right Path
sceneStructure: Setup: hero faces a decision with more than one apparent solution.
Choice A: a plausible but incomplete option is tried or seriously considered, and shown to fall short.
Choice B: a better option is tried, but it creates a new problem of its own.
Reflection: hero pauses to think about what both A and B were missing.
Choice C: the option that requires understanding the true belief is found and taken.
Resolution: Choice C works fully, and the difference between it and A/B is made clear.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero encounters several solutions that each look reasonable, but only the option requiring the true belief is actually complete â€” the story is about judgment, not right-vs-wrong.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is in the sophistication of the wrong answers â€” Choice A is obviously incomplete, Choice B is genuinely tempting and nearly right, raising the difficulty of choosing correctly.
templates.turningPoint: The reflection beat between Choice B and Choice C â€” the hero must articulate (even briefly) what both prior choices were missing before Choice C can be found.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must show why Choice C succeeds where A and B could not, directly connected to the true belief, not just narrated as 'the right one'.

templates.name: Lost â†’ Notice â†’ Found
sceneStructure: Loss: hero loses something important, framed through the false belief (the object feels essential to being okay).
Search begins: hero starts searching, focused entirely on the object.
Notice something else: mid-search, hero notices something unrelated â€” a clue, another character's need, or the symbol.
Deeper discovery: following that notice leads to something more meaningful than the object itself.
Object found: the original object is found, often almost incidentally, once the hero is no longer searching so anxiously.
Resolution: hero realizes the deeper discovery, not the object, is what actually mattered â€” the true belief is spoken.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero loses something important, and while searching for it notices something else entirely (a clue, another's need, a symbol, something about themselves); the original object is eventually found, but the deeper discovery is the real resolution.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is anxiety-based during the search, then quietly de-escalates once the deeper discovery begins â€” the emotional shape is tension releasing, not building further.
templates.turningPoint: The 'notice something else' beat â€” this must interrupt the search itself, pulling hero attention away from the object toward something more meaningful.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must explicitly rank the deeper discovery above the found object â€” the object's return is satisfying but secondary.

templates.name: Pass It On
sceneStructure: Hero receives: hero, struggling under the false belief, is helped by someone else.
Learning: hero reflects, even briefly, on what that help felt like.
Other struggles: later, a different character faces a recognizably similar struggle to the hero's original one.
Recall help: hero remembers the help they received and recognizes the parallel.
Hero gives: hero offers that same kind of help to the other character.
Resolution: hero's own understanding is completed by having given, not just received, and the true belief is spoken.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero receives help early in the story; later, another character faces a similar problem, and the hero remembers the help they received and passes it forward â€” beginning as a receiver, ending as a giver.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is relational, not physical â€” the story builds through widening the hero's circle of care from self to other.
templates.turningPoint: The recall-help beat, where the hero consciously connects the other character's struggle to their own earlier experience.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution requires the hero to actively give help (an action), not merely feel sympathy â€” sympathy alone is not sufficient for this template.

templates.name: The Unexpected Helper
sceneStructure: Problem: hero faces the obstacle and needs help.
Assumption: hero identifies who/what seems capable of helping, and dismisses another character or thing as unable to help â€” this is the false belief made concrete.
Dismissal: hero tries without the dismissed helper, and it is not enough.
Second look: hero is prompted (by circumstance or by the dismissed character themselves) to reconsider.
Unexpected contribution: the dismissed character/thing contributes exactly the missing piece, in a way true to their own nature.
Resolution: hero succeeds because of the unexpected helper, and openly acknowledges the assumption was wrong.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero assumes someone or something cannot possibly help; that assumption must be actively overcome before the supposedly unlikely helper contributes the missing piece the hero needed all along.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is in how firmly the assumption is held â€” the dismissal should feel reasonable/understandable to a young reader, not silly, so the reversal has real weight.
templates.turningPoint: The second-look beat, where the hero is willing to reconsider the dismissed character even without proof yet that they can help.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must make the unexpected helper's contribution feel true to who they are, not a random lucky ability â€” the story should honor that character's own nature.

templates.name: The Secret Mission
sceneStructure: Mission given: hero receives a small, seemingly simple mission.
Clue 1: hero finds the first clue toward completing it.
Obstacle 1: something gets in the way, tied to the false belief.
Clue 2: hero finds a second clue, which begins to hint the mission means more than expected.
Obstacle 2: a harder obstacle, testing the hero's commitment now that stakes feel higher.
Revelation: the mission's true, more meaningful purpose becomes clear.
Resolution: hero completes the mission understanding its real significance, true belief spoken.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero receives a small mission that unfolds through clue-obstacle-clue-obstacle beats, and the mission turns out to mean something more emotionally significant than the hero expected when they set out.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is both practical (Obstacle 2 harder than Obstacle 1) and emotional (the mission's stakes grow from small errand to something that matters).
templates.turningPoint: The revelation beat, placed after Obstacle 2, where the small mission is reframed as meaningful.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must complete the ORIGINAL small mission, now understood in its full meaning â€” the mission itself should not change, only its significance.

templates.name: The Growing Problem
sceneStructure: Tiny problem: a small, easy-to-dismiss problem appears.
Ignored: hero (driven by the false belief) ignores or reacts carelessly to it.
Grows 1: the problem grows larger as a direct consequence of being ignored.
Grows 2: it grows again, now visibly harder to ignore, feeding on the hero's reactions.
Overwhelming: the problem reaches its largest, most overwhelming size.
Pause: hero stops reacting entirely â€” the pause craft technique.
Real problem: underneath the now-huge problem, hero identifies the small, real, original issue.
Resolution: hero addresses the real (small) problem directly, and the overwhelming version dissolves.

repetitionPattern.phrase/source: a short description of the growing problem's size/shape, restated with the same sentence structure each time it grows
repetitionPattern.variationRule: each restatement must use the same sentence pattern with an intensified word/image (e.g. 'a small cloud' â†’ 'a big cloud' â†’ 'a cloud that filled the whole sky'), so the growth is felt rhythmically
repetitionPattern.finalVariation: at the pause beat, the growth pattern is explicitly broken â€” the next line does not describe the problem getting even bigger, it describes the hero stopping

templates.storyMechanic: A tiny problem is ignored, then grows larger and larger through repeated escalation, until the hero pauses instead of continuing to react, and identifies the real, smaller problem underneath the now-overwhelming one.
templates.escalationPattern: This IS the escalation template â€” the growing problem should visibly double or intensify at each stage, feeding specifically on being ignored/reacted-to rather than addressed.
templates.turningPoint: The pause beat, placed at the problem's largest point â€” the hero must stop reacting entirely before the real, smaller problem can be seen.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution requires showing that the real problem was small all along â€” the 'growth' was created by avoidance, not by the problem's true size.

templates.name: Choice at the Crossroads
sceneStructure: Approach crossroads: hero arrives at a moment where two paths are both genuinely available.
Option (old belief): the tempting, easier option is shown, clearly connected to the false belief.
Option (new belief): the harder option is shown, clearly connected to the true belief, without being obviously 'the right answer' yet.
Choice: hero chooses, deliberately and visibly, rather than drifting into a decision.
Consequence: the choice has a real, specific consequence â€” not simply praise for choosing well.
Resolution: the consequence resolves in a way that affirms the true belief, completing the mission.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero reaches a single, genuine choice between two options, each representing a different belief; choosing the harder, true-belief option must carry a real consequence, or the transformation will feel unearned.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation is in how genuinely tempting the old-belief option is made to feel â€” if it is not a real temptation, the choice beat has no weight.
templates.turningPoint: The choice beat itself is the turning point â€” everything before builds toward it, everything after is consequence.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution must follow logically and specifically from the exact choice made, so the story teaches that choices have real consequences, not just good feelings.

templates.name: Return With Something New
sceneStructure: Departure: hero leaves the familiar place, carrying the false belief with them.
Challenge: hero faces a real difficulty away from home, distinct from the original situation.
Discovery: hero finds something (a skill, an idea, a symbol) they did not have before.
Transformation: hero internalizes the discovery as the true belief.
Return: hero comes back to the original, familiar place.
Echo ending: the final scene deliberately mirrors the departure scene's setting and framing, but the hero now acts from the true belief within it.
templates.storyMechanic: The hero leaves familiar surroundings, is changed by a journey of challenge and discovery, and returns to the same starting place â€” the final scene deliberately echoes the opening, but the hero now behaves differently within it.
templates.escalationPattern: Escalation runs across the whole outward journey (challenge growing harder, discovery deepening into transformation) before resolving back at home.
templates.turningPoint: The transformation beat, placed just before the return, so the hero comes home already changed rather than being changed by arriving home.
templates.resolutionPattern: Resolution is the echo ending itself â€” the same place as the opening, now inhabited differently, proving mastery/resilience gained through the journey.
